chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the deranged one who has lost his intellect: Is his divorce allowed? He said: No. And about the woman when she is like that: Is her selling or her charity (gift) allowed? He said: No.

key_terms.الذَّاهِبِ الْعَقْلِ: The one who has lost his intellect

ai.seo_question: Is the divorce of an insane person valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the divorce of the insane (al-ma'tūh) is not valid, and their property cannot be sold or given in charity, indicating a lack of independent legal agency (ahliyyah) due to the absence of intellect. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that mental capacity is a prerequisite for valid legal acts, distinguishing the insane from those with minor cognitive impairments. The narration highlights the guardian's role in managing affairs, yet emphasizes that the core legal acts require the presence of sound mind.
